chunks.heading: Manifest Format
chunks.text: --- title: "Building Apps" description: "How to create a pyComputer application" --- An app is a directory with this structure: ```text myapp/ manifest.json main.py ... ``` ```json { "name": "myapp", "version": "0.1.0", "entry": "main.py", "permissions": ["fs"], "description": "My awesome app." } ``` Fields: - `name` - unique identifier (used by `pkg install` and `run`) - `version` - semver string - `entry` - Python file to load (relative to app directory) - `permissions` - list of permissions (`"fs"` for filesystem access) - `description` - human-readable summary

chunks.heading: Entry Point
chunks.text: `run`) - `version` - semver string - `entry` - Python file to load (relative to app directory) - `permissions` - list of permissions (`"fs"` for filesystem access) - `description` - human-readable summary The entry point file must export a `main()` function: ```python from pycomputersdk import Renderer from pycomputersdk.std import input, info, error r = Renderer() def main(*args): r.clear() r.banner("My App") name = input("Enter your name: ") if name: info(f"Hello, {name}!") else: error("No name entered.") ```

chunks.heading: Testing Locally
chunks.text: pycomputersdk import Renderer from pycomputersdk.std import input, info, error r = Renderer() def main(*args): r.clear() r.banner("My App") name = input("Enter your name: ") if name: info(f"Hello, {name}!") else: error("No name entered.") ``` Use the SDK CLI to run an app directly: ```bash pycomp run /path/to/myapp ``` Or inside pyComputer: ```bash cd pyComputer/pyComputer uv run python main.py [/] $ pkg install /path/to/myapp [/] $ run myapp ```

chunks.heading: Testing
chunks.text: SDK CLI to run an app directly: ```bash pycomp run /path/to/myapp ``` Or inside pyComputer: ```bash cd pyComputer/pyComputer uv run python main.py [/] $ pkg install /path/to/myapp [/] $ run myapp ``` The SDK provides test utilities in `pycomputersdk.testing`: ```python from pycomputersdk.testing import MockRenderer, MockInput, assert_screen def test_my_app(): mock = MockRenderer() mock.write("Hello") assert mock.capture() == "Hello" ``` Run tests with `pycomp test`: ```bash pycomp test . # run all tests pycomp test . -v # verbose mode pycomp test . -- tests/test_main.py # specific test file ``` The `pycomp init` scaffold creates a `tests/test_main.py` with `MockRenderer` and `MockInput` already wired up.

chunks.heading: CLI Workflow
chunks.text: tests pycomp test . -v # verbose mode pycomp test . -- tests/test_main.py # specific test file ``` The `pycomp init` scaffold creates a `tests/test_main.py` with `MockRenderer` and `MockInput` already wired up. The `pycomp` CLI provides a full development workflow: ```bash pycomp init myapp # Scaffold a new app project cd myapp pycomp validate . # Validate the manifest pycomp run . # Run the app in kernel environment pycomp test . # Run tests pycomp build . # Build .pycapp archive ```

chunks.heading: Packaging
chunks.text: myapp pycomp validate . # Validate the manifest pycomp run . # Run the app in kernel environment pycomp test . # Run tests pycomp build . # Build .pycapp archive ``` Use `pycomp build` to create a `.pycapp` archive: ```bash pycomp build . ``` Or inside pyComputer: ```bash [/] $ pkg build myapp ``` Or use the Python API directly: ```python from pycomputersdk.pkg import bundle result_path, digest = bundle("myapp", source_dir="/path/to/myapp") ``` The `.pycapp` is a ZIP file containing all app files plus `manifest.json`. The build command prints a SHA-256 hash for integrity verification.

chunks.text: pyComputer ships with six apps pre-installed under `root/usr/apps/`: Calculator : A four-function calculator with keyboard input support. IDE : A full TUI code editor with file tree, toolbar, syntax highlighting, and a run output panel. Matrix : Matrix-style digital rain animation. Notes : A plain-text note taker backed by the VFS. Settings : Configure the system theme, set your username, and adjust other preferences. Snake : Classic snake game with keyboard controls. ---

chunks.text: build . ``` Or using the `bundle()` function directly: ```python from pycomputersdk.pkg import bundle result_path, digest = bundle("myapp", source_dir="/path/to/myapp") ``` ```bash [/] $ pkg install path/to/myapp.pycapp [/] $ pkg install https://example.com/myapp.pycapp ``` When installing a `.pycapp` archive or downloading from a URL, `pkg install` validates: - The manifest is valid JSON and conforms to the Manifest schema - The app name does not contain path separators or `..` - Each extracted file stays within the destination directory (no path traversal) - Remote URLs require HTTPS For plain directory installs (`pkg install /path/to/dir`), only the manifest is validated; the directory is copied as-is without additional security checks.

chunks.heading: Boot Sequence
chunks.text: --- title: "Boot Sequence" description: "What happens when pyComputer starts" ---

chunks.heading: Step 1: Data Disk Initialization
chunks.text: --- title: "Boot Sequence" description: "What happens when pyComputer starts" --- `ensure_data_dir()` checks if `data/` exists. If not, it creates the data disk from the golden master (`root/`): 1. Create staging directory `data.staging/` 2. Copy `root/` → `data.staging/` with `shutil.copytree` 3. Atomic rename `data.staging/` → `data/` This guarantees that if the copy is interrupted, `data/` will not exist and initialization will retry on the next boot.

chunks.heading: Step 2: Settings Load

Loads `data/apps/settings/config.json` for theme, username, and preferences. Falls back to defaults if the file is missing.

chunks.heading: Architecture
chunks.text: --- title: "Architecture" description: "pyComputer architecture overview" --- pyComputer is organized into several subsystems that initialize in sequence at boot.

chunks.heading: Subsystems
chunks.text: --- title: "Architecture" description: "pyComputer architecture overview" --- pyComputer is organized into several subsystems that initialize in sequence at boot. ```mermaid flowchart TB Boot["Boot"] --> Kernel["Kernel"] Kernel --> VFS["VFS"] Kernel --> Shell["Shell"] Kernel --> SDK["SDK"] Shell --> Pkg["Package Manager"] SDK --> Net["Network"] Boot -.->|Logo, hardware init, data disk setup| Boot Kernel -.->|Scheduler, IO, Loader, Registry| Kernel VFS -.->|Virtual filesystem, path mapping| VFS Shell -.->|Command loop, built-in commands, app launcher| Shell SDK -.->|Public API for app development| SDK Net -.->|HTTP client, JSON helpers| Net Pkg -.->|Manager, bundler, manifest validation| Pkg style Boot fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style Kernel fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style VFS fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style Shell fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style SDK fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style Net fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style Pkg fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 ```

chunks.heading: Initialization Order
chunks.text: client, JSON helpers| Net Pkg -.->|Manager, bundler, manifest validation| Pkg style Boot fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style Kernel fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style VFS fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style Shell fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style SDK fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style Net fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 style Pkg fill:#1c1917,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fafaf9 ``` 1. `ensure_data_dir()` - copies `root/` to `data/` if `data/` does not exist (atomic staging) 2. `_load_settings()` - loads theme and user preferences 3. Theme setup - applies the configured theme via `set_theme()` 4. `_require_login()` - if a `password` setting exists, prompts for credentials before continuing 5. `Kernel()` - creates all subsystems 6. `kernel.initialize()` - prints init messages 7. `kernel.boot_sequence()` - renders logo and hardware logs 8. `kernel.launch_shell()` - starts shell event loop 9. `asyncio.run(kernel.run())` - main async event loop

chunks.heading: Kernel
chunks.text: --- title: "Kernel" description: "pyComputer kernel architecture" --- The kernel is the central coordinator. It owns all subsystems and manages the event loop.

chunks.heading: Components
chunks.text: --- title: "Kernel" description: "pyComputer kernel architecture" --- The kernel is the central coordinator. It owns all subsystems and manages the event loop. | Component | Responsibility | |-------------|-------------------------------------------------------| | `Kernel` | Orchestrator, creates subsystems, runs event loop | | `Scheduler` | Async task scheduler based on `asyncio` | | `IO` | I/O multiplexing | | `Loader` | App discovery, manifest loading, dynamic imports | | `Registry` | Installed app database (persisted to `sys/apps.json`) |

chunks.heading: Loader
chunks.text: task scheduler based on `asyncio` | | `IO` | I/O multiplexing | | `Loader` | App discovery, manifest loading, dynamic imports | | `Registry` | Installed app database (persisted to `sys/apps.json`) | The loader discovers apps by scanning `usr/apps/` for directories containing `manifest.json`. It uses `importlib` to dynamically import app entry points, temporarily adding the app directory to `sys.path`. ```text discover_apps() → scan usr/apps/ for manifest.json files import_entrypoint(name) → read manifest, load main.py, return main() import_from_path(path) → load app from any directory ```

chunks.heading: Registry
chunks.text: points, temporarily adding the app directory to `sys.path`. ```text discover_apps() → scan usr/apps/ for manifest.json files import_entrypoint(name) → read manifest, load main.py, return main() import_from_path(path) → load app from any directory ``` The registry tracks installed apps in `sys/apps.json`. It is a simple JSON array of app names. ```json ["calculator", "notes", "glyphformer"] ```

The VFS root depends on the environment: | Environment | Root Path | |------------------------|--------------------------------| | `PYCOMPUTER_DATA_DIR` | Value of the environment var | | Native (macOS/Linux) | `<project>/../data` | | Web (Pyodide) | `/root` or `/pyComputer/root` |

chunks.text: the environment: | Environment | Root Path | |------------------------|--------------------------------| | `PYCOMPUTER_DATA_DIR` | Value of the environment var | | Native (macOS/Linux) | `<project>/../data` | | Web (Pyodide) | `/root` or `/pyComputer/root` | ```python vfs = VFS() vfs.abspath("usr/apps") # → /path/to/data/usr/apps vfs.abspath("sys/conf.json") # → /path/to/data/sys/conf.json vfs.abspath("/boot/logo.txt") # → /path/to/data/boot/logo.txt ```

chunks.text: | | Native (macOS/Linux) | `<project>/../data` | | Web (Pyodide) | `/root` or `/pyComputer/root` | ```python vfs = VFS() vfs.abspath("usr/apps") # → /path/to/data/usr/apps vfs.abspath("sys/conf.json") # → /path/to/data/sys/conf.json vfs.abspath("/boot/logo.txt") # → /path/to/data/boot/logo.txt ``` | Method | Implementation | |---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------| | `abspath(path)` | Joins with root, normalizes | | `open(path, mode)` | `open(self.abspath(path), mode)` | | `read(path)` | Reads entire file as string | | `write(path, data)` | Writes string to file | | `exists(path)` | `os.path.exists(self.abspath(path))` | | `mkdir(path)` | `os.makedirs(self.abspath(path), exist_ok=True)` | | `remove(path)` | Removes file or directory tree | | `move(src, dst)` | `shutil.move(self.abspath(src), self.abspath(dst))` |
--- title: "Core Concepts" description: "How pyComputer works" ---

chunks.heading: Core Concepts
chunks.text: --- title: "Core Concepts" description: "How pyComputer works" ---

chunks.heading: Golden Master & Data Disk
chunks.text: --- title: "Core Concepts" description: "How pyComputer works" --- pyComputer has a two-disk model: - `root/` - The **golden master**. Version-controlled, read-only at runtime. Contains pre-installed apps, system config, boot assets. - `data/` - The **runtime disk**. Created fresh from the golden master on first boot. All runtime modifications (installed apps, settings) go here. This means you can always reset to factory state by deleting `data/`.

chunks.heading: Virtual Filesystem (VFS)
chunks.text: The **runtime disk**. Created fresh from the golden master on first boot. All runtime modifications (installed apps, settings) go here. This means you can always reset to factory state by deleting `data/`. The VFS is a thin wrapper around the real filesystem. It maps VFS paths (like `usr/apps`) to real paths under `data/`. Apps use the VFS to read/write files without knowing where they are stored. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph VFS["VFS Path"] A1["/usr/apps"] A2["/sys/apps.json"] A3["boot/logo.txt"] end subgraph Real["Real Path"] B1["data/usr/apps"] B2["data/sys/apps.json"] B3["data/boot/logo.txt"] end A1 --> B1 A2 --> B2 A3 --> B3 ```

chunks.heading: App Model
chunks.text: knowing where they are stored. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph VFS["VFS Path"] A1["/usr/apps"] A2["/sys/apps.json"] A3["boot/logo.txt"] end subgraph Real["Real Path"] B1["data/usr/apps"] B2["data/sys/apps.json"] B3["data/boot/logo.txt"] end A1 --> B1 A2 --> B2 A3 --> B3 ``` Apps are Python projects with a `manifest.json`. They can be: - **Pre-installed** - shipped in `root/usr/apps/` - **Installed** - added via `pkg install` to `data/usr/apps/` - **Packed** - distributed as `.pycapp` archives (ZIP files) Each app has an entry point (`main.py` by default) that exports a `main()` function. The shell's `run` command discovers and loads apps dynamically.

chunks.heading: Package Manager
chunks.text: - **Packed** - distributed as `.pycapp` archives (ZIP files) Each app has an entry point (`main.py` by default) that exports a `main()` function. The shell's `run` command discovers and loads apps dynamically. `pkg` is the built-in package manager. It handles: - `pkg install <path|url|name>` - install from local dir, `.pycapp` URL, or registry - `pkg remove <name>` - uninstall - `pkg search [term]` - browse registry - `pkg build <name>` - create `.pycapp` archives - `pkg registry [url]` - configure registry URL

chunks.heading: SDK
chunks.text: URL, or registry - `pkg remove <name>` - uninstall - `pkg search [term]` - browse registry - `pkg build <name>` - create `.pycapp` archives - `pkg registry [url]` - configure registry URL The `pycomputersdk` package provides the API and tooling for building standalone apps: - `Renderer` - TUI rendering (box-drawing, themes, ANSI output) - `get_key()`, `Key`, `pyc_input` - keyboard and text input handling - `std.*` - standard library (input, info, error, confirm, dialogs) - `VFS` - filesystem access from within apps - `testing.*` - `MockRenderer`, `MockInput`, `assert_screen` for unit testing - `pkg.*` - `Manifest`, `bundle()` for programmatic app packaging - `logging.*` - structured logging with levels - `net.*` - `HTTP` client - `async_utils.*` - async utilities (debounce, throttle, BackgroundTask, etc.) The `pycomp` CLI provides a full development workflow: ```bash pycomp init myapp # scaffold a new app pycomp validate . # validate the manifest pycomp run . # run the app pycomp test . # run tests pycomp build . # package as .pycapp ```

chunks.heading: Shell
chunks.text: scaffold a new app pycomp validate . # validate the manifest pycomp run . # run the app pycomp test . # run tests pycomp build . # package as .pycapp ``` The shell is a command-line interface with: - Built-in commands (`ls`, `cat`, `edit`, `run`, `pkg`, etc.) - Command history (via readline) - Tab completion - The pyc_input() function for cross-platform input

chunks.heading: SDK Reference
chunks.text: --- title: "SDK Reference" description: "pyComputer SDK reference" --- The `pycomputersdk` package provides the public API for building pyComputer apps. It re-exports from `pycomputer.*` modules and includes a CLI tool for scaffolding, building, running, and testing apps.

chunks.heading: Installation
chunks.text: "pyComputer SDK reference" --- The `pycomputersdk` package provides the public API for building pyComputer apps. It re-exports from `pycomputer.*` modules and includes a CLI tool for scaffolding, building, running, and testing apps. Clone the repo and install with uv: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NellowTCS/pyComputer cd pyComputer/pyComputerSDK uv pip install -e . ``` Or from PyPI: ```bash uv pip install pycomputersdk ``` Or with pip: ```bash cd pyComputerSDK pip install -e . ```

chunks.heading: Package Structure
chunks.text: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NellowTCS/pyComputer cd pyComputer/pyComputerSDK uv pip install -e . ``` Or from PyPI: ```bash uv pip install pycomputersdk ``` Or with pip: ```bash cd pyComputerSDK pip install -e . ``` ```text pycomputersdk/ __init__.py - Renderer, Key, VFS, utility exports std.py - Standard library (input, info, error, etc.) fs.py - VFS re-export logging.py - Logger, Level, level functions net.py - HTTP client pkg.py - Manifest, bundle, ManifestError testing.py - MockRenderer, MockInput, assert_screen async_utils.py - debounce, throttle, with_timeout, BackgroundTask, etc. cli/ main.py - pycomp CLI entry point commands/ init.py - Scaffold a new app project build.py - Build a .pycapp archive validate.py - Validate app manifest test.py - Run app tests with pytest run.py - Run an app in a full kernel environment root/ - Template root filesystem (logo, apps.json, motd) ```

chunks.heading: CLI Tool
chunks.text: archive validate.py - Validate app manifest test.py - Run app tests with pytest run.py - Run an app in a full kernel environment root/ - Template root filesystem (logo, apps.json, motd) ``` The SDK provides the `pycomp` CLI for app development: ```bash pycomp init myapp # Scaffold a new app pycomp validate . # Validate app manifest pycomp run . # Run app in kernel environment pycomp build . # Build .pycapp archive pycomp test . # Run app tests ```

chunks.heading: Workspace
chunks.text: app pycomp validate . # Validate app manifest pycomp run . # Run app in kernel environment pycomp build . # Build .pycapp archive pycomp test . # Run app tests ``` The repo uses a uv workspace with two members, managed by the root `pyproject.toml`: ```toml [tool.uv.workspace] members = ["pyComputer", "pyComputerSDK"] ```
